column2: The teacher should make a mandala for the sake of initiation and for taking a mantra; a lotus with the front sunlike and the moon-divided, in two parts, is beneficial.
A path and a border should be made; eight lotuses in a four-square; the path and border outside; the doors two-square;
and two sub-doors, a corner-bond, double border; nine white lotuses; the pericarp gold-bright;
the filaments various; one should fill the corners with red; the space between the sky-lines black; the doors by the elephant measure.
In the middle lotus Sarasvati; Vagishi in the east lotus; Hrillekha, Chitra-Vagishi, Gayatri, Vishvarupa;

Shankari, Mati and Dhriti from the east, with the "hrim" seed of their own, to be meditated like Sarasvati; an oblation with tawny-cow ghee; he becomes a poet in Sanskrit and Prakrit, a knower of poetics and the sciences.
One should turn it back by half the joint-thread; the sharp-pointed lotus with good wind gives enjoyment and liberation.
In increase of enjoyment and in subjugation, a "bala" lotus equal; nine-navel, nine-cubit, by mantra-formed parts;
in the middle a lotus, the seed of the border; by the door by the lotus measure; with neck and near-neck omitted; outside it a path is held;
it is five-parted, and ten-parted all around; in the directions and corners eight lotuses, a door-lotus with path;
outside it, five borders where the path is adorned; the door-neck like a lotus, with border, lip-neck;
the cheek-border should be made; three doors clear in the directions; corner-bond three-leaved, double-banded like a thunderbolt.
The middle lotus white, yellow, red and blue; yellow-white and smoky, red and yellow — giving liberation.
Eight lotuses in the east and so on; one should recite Shiva, Vishnu and the rest. Having worshipped in the middle of the temple, Indra and the rest on the lotuses and so on;
the weapons on the outer path; one who worships Vishnu and the rest obtains the Ashvamedha. At the mounting of the purifier (pavitra) and the rest one should draw the great mandala.
An eight-cubit field first, one should turn it with the sixfold sides; a two-square lotus in the middle, then path and border;
then in directions and corners eight blue lotuses one should draw; by the measure of the middle lotus thirty lotuses;
without petal-joints, blue water-lilies; at its back the border, path, swastikas above it;
two-square and eight, made in square portions; one should draw swastikas there, the path outside as before;
doors as the lotus with near-neck; the corner red, the path yellow, the lotus in the mandala blue;
swastika and the rest variegated, giving all desires, Guha. A five-lotus of five cubits, divided tenfold all around;
a two-square lotus, path, border, lotus in the directions; a four at the back, path, border, two-square otherwise;
with neck and near-neck the doors, the lotus in the middle. In this five-lotus mandala white and yellow earlier,
the south lotus beryl-bright, the west lotus jasmine-bright; the north lotus conch-bright; the rest all variegated.
I shall tell the mandala giving all desires, of ten cubits; divided by changes, four-cornered, the door two-square;
in the middle a lotus as before; now I tell the destroyer of obstacles: having made a four-cubit city and a circle of two cubits,
a path of one cubit surrounded by many swastikas; doors of a cubit in the corners, a circle with lotus;
five white lotuses; in the middle the partless is to be worshipped; the heart and the rest in the east and so on; in the corners one should worship the weapons;
as before the five Brahmas; then I tell the basis of intelligence: in a hundred parts or fifteen parts a lotus, eight lingas in a direction;
joined with a girdle part, the neck two-square. The teacher should arrange creepers and the rest by his intellect;
four, six, five, eight and so on, the mandala of "kha-chikha" and so on; all going to "kha-akshi, moon, sun," by the description of the moon;
fourteen hundred and forty are the mandalas of Hari, Shambhu, the Goddess and the Sun.
When divided by ten and seven, hear the creeper-linga born: five, three and one in directions, three and five one should omit;
in the upward two-square, the linga temple at side compartments; in the middle a two-square lotus, and one lotus;
on both sides of the linga, in the Bhadra, by non-omission of the foot-door; six side-shows omitted, creepers the rest and of Hari;
having omitted the upward two-square, Hari's eight Bhadras are remembered; adorned with omission of the Veda joined with ray-measure;
a twenty-five lotus, then a seat without seat; guarding two and two, and eight sub-ornaments;
the Bhadra that announces the Goddess and the rest, large in the middle, small beyond; in the middle a nine-square lotus, at the corner four Bhadras;
the remainder thirteen-square, the mandala of intelligence-basis; hundred-petalled, over sixty, the intelligence-basis in Hara and the rest.
With ghee, by a lakh falling (oblations), it is beneficial in earth-born portents. In ghee and guggulu oblation it crushes all portents and the like;
by oblation of durva, unbroken rice and ghee, diseases; and with ghee by a thousand bad dreams perish, no doubt;
by ten thousand it destroys planetary fault, mixed with hibiscus and ghee; for pacifying Vinayaka's trouble ten thousand of ghee;
peace from spirits and vetalas by ten thousand of guggulu. On breaking of a great tree, a snake and heron staying in the house,
on entry of wild animals, by offering durva, ghee and rice; on meteors and earthquake, by oblation of sesame and ghee there is welfare;
on bleeding of trees, by ten thousand of guggulu welfare; on unseasonal fruits and flowers, on breaking of the kingdom and in killing,
when there is epidemic among bipeds and the rest, by half a lakh of sesame and ghee; for pacification of elephant-epidemic, in growth of a female elephant's tusks,
in a female elephant and in seeing rut, peace is desired by ten thousand. In untimely miscarriage, where what is born perishes,
where deformed ones are born, at time of journey one should offer ten thousand; a lakh of sesame-ghee oblation for the best success;

in the middle half of that, and a quarter in the lowest; as the recitation so the oblation; in battle there would be victory. One should recite the Aghora weapon, having placed and meditated on the powerful five-faced.
Having recited thirty times, it should be given among thieves; with powdered white teeth, fallen, for purification.

Om, blazing-eyed, with tawny matted locks, shining, scatterer, Trailokyadamara, dara dara, bhrama bhrama, akatta akatta, totaya totaya, motaya motaya, daha daha, pacha pacha — thus the accomplished Rudra commands: "If the seizer has gone to heaven or the world of gods or to a pleasure-park mountain, still I shall bring him back; take the offering, take, I give to you, svaha." Having given the field-guardian offering, the seizer goes to the place of restraint. Enemies meet destruction; in battle the host of foes is destroyed.
Having placed the Hamsa seed one would remove threefold poison. Agaru, sandal, kushtha, saffron, nagakesara,
nail-perfume and devadaru in equal parts as incense, joined with honey, by fumigating body, clothes and the like,
it is auspicious in dispute, bewildering women, in strife and quarrel; in choosing a maiden for good fortune, consecrated with the Maya mantra.
Hrim — gorochana, nagakesara flowers, saffron and realgar; having made a tilaka on the forehead, whomever one sees becomes subject.
Powder of shatavari drunk with milk gives a son; powder of nagakesara cooked in ghee gives a son;
by drinking palasha seeds one gets a son. "Om rise, Chamunda, jambhaya" — twenty-six (syllables), that accomplished knowledge, with clay from a river bank for a woman,
having made her, and having written the name on an arka leaf with datura juice, then having urinated, one should recite and bring the woman.

Om kshum sah vashat — the Mahamrityunjaya mantra gives nourishment by recitation and oblation. "Om hamsah hrum hum sa hrah saum" — the Mritasanjivani knowledge, eight-lettered, gives victory in battle.
Mantras headed by Ishana give dharma, desire and the rest. Ishana is lord of all knowledges, of all beings,

lord of Brahma, Brahman: may Shiva, Sadashiva, be mine. "Om, we know Tatpurusha; we meditate on Mahadeva; may that Rudra impel us." "Om to the Aghoras and the Ghoras, to the Ghora-removers on all sides,

homage to all, to the Rudra forms. Om homage to Vamadeva; homage to the eldest; homage to Rudra; to Kala; to Kalavikarana; to Balavikarana; to Balapramathana; to Sarvabhutadamana; to Manonmana." "Om, I shall tell Sadyojata: homage to Sadyojata. In birth after birth, in the beginningless birth, worship me, origin of existence."

I shall tell the five Brahmas and the six limbs, giving enjoyment and liberation: "Om homage to the Supreme Self, the Beyond, giver of desires, to the Supreme Lord, to Yoga, to the Source of Yoga, to the Maker of all — make the heart giver of all aims, endowed with seventy syllables. Om Shiva, homage to Shiva, Shiva. Om, in the heart, Jvalini svaha, the crest. Om, Shiva-nature, great splendor, all-knowing, lord, turn back, great terrible, armor, tawny, homage. Great armor, by Shiva's command bind the heart, bind, whirl whirl, crush crush, bearer of fine thunderbolt, thunderbolt-noose, bow, thunderbolt-lightning, thunderbolt-bodied, entering my body, stop all wicked ones, stop, hum." The armor of the letters is a hundred and five syllables.
In stopping, smoky; in banishing and killing, black-colored; in drawing, tawny; in bewildering one should worship the thirty-two-colored.
One should recite the mantra thirty lakh and offer a tenth; with guggulu and amrita, accomplished or not, it does all.
There is no mantra other than Aghora that gives enjoyment and liberation. A non-celibate becomes celibate, an unbathed becomes a bather.
The Aghora-weapon and Aghora — these two are kings of mantras. By recitation, oblation and worship in battle one would crush the enemy army.
I shall tell the Rudra-peace, auspicious, accomplishing all aims: for a son, for destroying planets, for destroying poison and disease,
for peace of famine and epidemic, for removing bad dreams, for obtaining strength and kingdom and for destroying enemies,
for a tree that fruits out of season, in crushing all seizers. In worship the salutation, ending with "svaha" in oblation;
in nourishing, "vashat"; in strengthening "vaushat" should be applied. In place of the two "cha" one should apply the species-yoga.

Om to Rudra... Om homage to the Bull; to the Avimukta, to the Unborn, to Purusha, to the Worshipful, to Ishana, to Paurusha, and five in the north; to Vishvarupa, to the Terrible, to the Deformed, to the Undeformed, the two deformed in the other time; to Kala; in the waters Maya; at southwest; to Ekapingala, to Shvetapingala, to Krishnapingala, homage; to Madhupingala; to Madhupingala in the Niyati; to Ananta; to the moist, to the dry; to the troop of waters; in the Time-principle; to Karala, to Vikarala — two in the Maya-principle; to Thousand-headed, thousand-faced, thousand-handed and -footed, thousand-lingaed — in the Vidya-principle. From the thousand-eyed one should place on the right plough; to Ekajata, to Dvijata, to Trijata svaha; to Kara, to Svadhakara, to Vashatkara, to Vashatkara, to the six Rudras — in the Isha-principle on the fire-leaf stationed, Guha. To the Lord of beings, Lord of animals, Lord of Uma, Overlord of Time; in the Sadashiva-overseer principle six are to be worshipped on the east petal. To Uma, of ugly form, Om do. Then in the west: Om dhri dhri nana vam vam, Anidhana, source of dissolution, Shiva, Supreme Self of all, Mahadeva, Lord of existence, great splendor, lord of yoga, release release, Pramatha, Om all, Om be, Om source of being, giver of happiness to all beings; in the wind-leaf, then in the Niyati, Purusha and north: maker of all presence, beyond Brahma, Vishnu and Rudra, unworshipped and unpraised, witness; (garbled syllables) knowledge, sound, subtle, Shiva, giver of all; Om homage to Shiva, Om homage homage to Shiva, Om homage homage — in the Ishana, in the Prakrita principle one should worship, offer and recite; it quiets planets, disease and illusion-distress and does all success.
On the ground the Matrika letters should be written, without conjuncts and eunuch-letters; having separated the mantra letters one should lead the anusvara separately;
of the practitioner, whatever his name, one should separate it; at the beginning and end of the mantra one should join the practitioner's letters;
Siddha, Sadhya, Susiddha, Ari — from the name one should reckon in order; at the beginning and end of the mantra it gives success, by a hundred parts.
